text:
jamal: Quick check — we just had a support ticket where SCIM removed a user immediately after their SSO orgUnit changed. App sessions stayed active and customer flagged it. What is our recommended deprovision grace window for SCIM -> app access? Also: do we log group display names in audit logs? Need redaction guidance. @ana
ana: short answer: policy is to avoid immediate teardown for non-high-priv users. We typically allow a 48h grace window before forcing token revocation, but high-priv groups (admin/infra) require immediate action + manual review. For logging: we should not persist plain group display names for >90 days in raw logs. Hash or redact.
jamal: got it. Is the 48h configured in the SCIM sync service or the session management layer?
mike: It's enforced in the session manager. SCIM sends the user.disabled event -> we mark user as deprovisioned, but session_killer waits grace_window before revoking unless the user is in an exception list. Exception list is populated from mapped "sensitive_groups" config.
sophie: For the logs, recommend storing group identifiers only as stable opaque ids (externalId) and hashing them in access logs. Eg we log `group_id: sha256(<externalId>)` instead of `group_name`. That keeps debugging workable without PII.
laura: +1. For audit retention we keep full SCIM audit entries in secure audit-store for 365 days but scrub display names in the hot logs. If someone needs the real name for an investigation, they request from security ops (ticket) and we unwrap with KMS.
jamal: can we show a small example of the SCIM PATCH we use and the log line before/after redaction? saves a support ping.
sophie: sure — example SCIM remove op we emit to the service bus:

```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "remove",
      "path": "members[value eq \"user-123\"]"
    }
  ]
}
```
laura: example log line (before):
`SCIM: user=user-123 removed from group=Payroll Contractors display_name=Payroll — src=scim-sync`
and (after redaction):
`SCIM: user=user-123 removed from group_id=sha256:3f2a... src=scim-sync`
ana: note — make sure the sha256 prefix is deterministic and we store the lookup table in the secure audit-store only. Also add an audit marker when a redaction lookup is performed (who/unlocked).
scim-bot: Audit: SCIM/patch applied user-123 -> group-id=3f2a... (redacted) ts=1876543300
jamal: ok this helps. Action items: 1) Sophie -> add hashing helper to scim-sync (PR), 2) Mike -> verify exception list has infra/admin groups, 3) Laura -> confirm timeline for access to secure audit-store for SRE when doing incident triage. I'll open a follow-up and tag owners. :thumbsup:
